sentences.text: "Cease fire, cease fire — misfire procedures, now," barked the master gunner, already sprinting down the catwalk. Her destroyer's camo rating is absurd; she vanished behind a single bush and deleted half my hitpoints. Formation looked ragged from the tower: second platoon drifting wide, kicking up its own brown wall. Behind the firing line, ammo handlers stack expended casings that still smoke at the mouth. Honestly, the stock grind on this medium hurts; forty rounds of low-pen AP against angled armor everywhere. Bro really sidescraped into a wall, ate two penetrations, and typed noob team in all chat. I'll wiggle my turret at the corner to bait his shot, then you cross the street on my call. Twelve seconds from target up to steel on steel — the standard the instructors wanted was under eight. Somewhere behind the smoke, a recovery vehicle idled, waiting for the first thrown track of the day. Someone explain why our top-tier heavy is sniping from spawn while three mediums hold the entire city flank. Dust boiled off the lead vehicle's tracks as the column wheeled left onto the gunnery lane. After the last run the chief instructor debriefed each crew beside the still-ticking engine decks. It was the coax bursts, not the main gun, that stitched the pop-up silhouettes flat. Column speed held at fifteen kph, per the safety brief, while the guns worked left to right. The 120mm report slammed across the range a full second before the target silhouette folded. We baited their whole platoon into the quarry, then Priya's medium clipped the artillery sitting naked at spawn. At three hundred meters, his upper glacis autobounces anything we carry, so aim for the cupola or the machine-gun port. Heat shimmer bent the horizon until the distant hulks looked like they were floating. Reloading, four seconds — hug the rubble and pray his gunner is asleep. Who queued us into an assault map with three open-topped destroyers and zero armor on the team? What is the meaning of the word tank?
